title: token-lifecycle-attrition-and-prepaid-slab-matching-notes
summary: Working sandbox to surface how customer token attrition shapes prepaid-slab sizing, internal headcount phasing, and GPU lease arbitrage. Focus is on building a pragmatic decision tile: when to shift customers to smaller slabs, when to top up credits, and how to time hiring to avoid stranded reserved capacity.
body:
Purpose / context:
- Quick model for matching prepaid credit slabs to observed token consumption lifecycles. Goal: reduce prepaid leakage while keeping slate simple for sales and minimizing churn risk.
- Tie headcount ramping (solutions + onboarding) to slab economics so hiring aligns with expected realized revenue rather than paper top-line.

Key assumptions (editable):
- Avg token price (list price) = $0.12 / 1k tokens (hosted blended)
- Typical customer initial slab sizes offered: 250k, 1M, 5M tokens
- Measured 6-month median attrition on new accounts = 42% (cohort May 2026)
- GPU lease arbitrage: short-term GPU spot/lease can shave $40k/mo per 8-GPU pod vs committed for burst windows

Live scenario table (rows = scenarios):
Scenario,Prepaid slab ($),Prepaid tokens,Effective $/1k,Peak-month-use (k),6mo realized tokens,Attrition,Headcount delta (FTE),GPU-lease savings/mo,Net realized rev ($)
Conservative,2000,16.6M,$0.12,220k,3.2M,80%,0,0,2400
Baseline,1000,8.3M,$0.12,180k,4.8M,42%,+0.5,8,5760
Aggressive,5000,41.6M,$0.12,900k,25.0M,40%,+2,40,30000
Flash-burst (promo),250,2.08M,$0.12,1,200k,1.2M,85%,-0.2,12,144

Notes on table: numbers are illustrative. "Prepaid tokens" = slab $ / $ per 1k * 1000. "6mo realized tokens" = cumulative tokens consumed in first 6 months after attrition applied. Net realized rev approximates $/1k * realized tokens minus estimated cost-to-serve (not included here).

Observations so far:
- Mid-tier slabs (1k USD) are the biggest source of leakage: cohorts show long tail of low usage after month 2, but sales prefers fixed slabs for simplicity.
- If attrition holds ~40%, prepaid leakage (unused tokens) equals ~40% of slab value for that cohort — meaningful for committed capacity planning.
- GPU-lease arbitrage helps smooth bursts for top customers; but requires operational overhead. If we gate lease to top 10% of customers by volume, it reduces committed capacity needs by ~6-8% in baseline.

Sensitivity checks (quick):
- Move attrition +/- 10 points: realized revenue for baseline swings +/- ~15%.
- Effective unit economics change if we compress slab sizes (more smaller slabs): on paper fewer unused tokens, but friction in sales & more churn risk during onboarding.

Headcount timing thought experiment:
- Current onboarding: 1 sales-engineer FTE per $1.2M of slab ARR (rough).
- If we shift to smaller slabs and higher churn, need +0.5 FTE per 6-month cohort to keep churn < 10% during ramp.
- Hiring lag is 8–10 weeks; propose a 2-week lead indicator derived from prepaid top-ups to trigger hiring approvals.

Open questions / To do:
- Pull detailed cohort token consumption by customer segment (enterprise vs mid-market vs startup) — Evan to add query (JIRA-FIN-4421).
- Add estimated cost-to-serve per 1k tokens by model family and region (needed to convert "Net realized rev" into margin).
- Run a simulation where we replace a 1M slab with two 500k micro-slabs priced with 5% premium; measure churn and average realized rev.
- Confirm legal implications for top-ups and refunds in APAC (Priya follow-up).

Quick decision tiles (recommendations for this draft):
- Short-term (1–3 months): pilot 500k micro-slab for a subset of self-serve accounts; instrument top-up triggers and one-click auto-refill. Monitor 60-day realized tokens.
- Medium-term (3–9 months): define FTE trigger thresholds: if prepaid top-ups exceed X% or cohort 60d realization < Y, hire +0.5 onboarding engineer.
- Capacity ops: allow SRE/infra to lease 1–2 short-term GPU pods for burst customers; estimate payback if pod used > 60% of month.

Action items (owners):
- Evan Liu: add cohort-level token consumption export + pivot table (due 2026-05-19).
- Priya Rao: legal/regional refund rules and billing language for micro-slabs (due 2026-05-26).
- Samir Das: simulate GPU-lease gating logic and run cost/savings model (due 2026-06-03).
- Maya Thompson (me): convert pilot assumptions into a small A/B experiment doc for sales ops (due 2026-06-08).

Notes to self (rough):
- Be careful: downstream billing complexity increases CS load. Keep a small-slip button: "auto-convert to larger slab after 2 top-ups" to reduce churn while minimizing leakage.
- Consider refundable trial credits for first 30 days to capture truth of demand without heavy prepaid exposure.

Revision log (simple):
- 2026-05-12: initial sandbox created (Maya)
- 2026-05-18: added sensitivity scenarios and headcount rules (Evan)
- 2026-05-25: updated legal follow-ups and tasks (Priya)

References / links:
- Pricing sim repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pricing-sim
- Related Confluence: CONFLUENCE-FAIRMATCH-78
- Jira: JIRA-FIN-4421

Unresolved risks:
- Sales pushback on too many slab SKUs (UX tax).
- Unexpected large variance in attrition for AI-native startups vs enterprise.
- GPU lease ops complexity creating throttles for high priority customers.

If this doc looks right I will convert to a small sheet with formulas and a slider for attrition + unit price.

-- Maya
notes: Informal working doc: mix of table, assumptions, action items. Not approved budget. Use as input to formal FY28 slab design if pilot metrics warrant.
